# A-2 · Assessment Plan

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Step | A Assess (system level) |
| Phases | PH-EMD (primary) |
| Depends on | A-1, I-2 |
| Inputs | ART-SSP, ART-BASELINE, ART-RA, ART-ORG-CONTEXT, EXT-ASSESSMENT-PROCEDURES, ART-REQ, EXT-TEST-STRATEGY |
| Outputs | ART-SAP (produces), ART-AUTHREC (produces) |
| Writes facts | — |
| Minimum interviews | 1 |
| RACI | R: PER-SCA, PER-AODR · A: PER-AO · C: PER-CISO, PER-PRIV, PER-PM, PER-CCP, PER-IO, PER-ISSM, PER-CDT, PER-OTA · I: — · PER-PRIV only when the system processes PII |
| Persona cards | [PER-SCA](../../personas/PER-SCA.md), [PER-AODR](../../personas/PER-AODR.md), [PER-AO](../../personas/PER-AO.md), [PER-CISO](../../personas/PER-CISO.md), [PER-PRIV](../../personas/PER-PRIV.md), [PER-PM](../../personas/PER-PM.md), [PER-CCP](../../personas/PER-CCP.md), [PER-IO](../../personas/PER-IO.md), [PER-ISSM](../../personas/PER-ISSM.md), [PER-CDT](../../personas/PER-CDT.md), [PER-OTA](../../personas/PER-OTA.md) |

Purpose: Develop, review and approve the security assessment plan, coordinated with developmental and operational test events, before the TRR for the first event that supplies assessment evidence.
<!-- END rmf:header -->
<!-- rmf:body authored -->

## Steps

1. **Entry check.** `uv run rmf status <run>` names A-2; S-4 is done (statements for every
   baseline control) and A-1 and I-2 are done or deferred. Why: the plan assesses the
   controls as the SSP documents them.
2. **Read the inputs** in `## Inputs`. For the methods, read the assessment objectives of
   the scoped controls with `uv run rmf catalog show --run <run> --fields title,objectives`
   (per family when the baseline is large).
3. **Interview PER-SCA** (`## Interviews`): approach, methods and objects per control, depth
   and coverage, reuse of developer and developmental test results, external providers, team
   and independence, schedule and test events, rules of engagement. Interview PER-PM on
   notification, resources and access: the system owner does these. Read ART-RA for the risk
   results the tailoring applies, and ART-ORG-CONTEXT for the organization's operations and
   its reuse policy.
4. **Write `artifacts/data/sap.yaml`** from `templates/data/sap.yaml`:
   - `scope.include: baseline` (the whole tailored baseline is in scope). List a control in
     `excluded_controls` only with a `rationale` the AODR accepted. Why: SAP-COV-001 checks
     that every baseline control is in scope or excluded with a reason.
   - `assessment_subjects`: the components (`type: component`, `include: all` or a list of
     `CMP-*` IDs) and inventory items to examine and test.
   - `team`: at least the lead assessor (`persona: PER-SCA`, `role`, `independent: true`
     when the assessor is organizationally independent of the program), each with a
     `qualification` the CISO verified. `assessor_independence`: the degree the AO determined
     (`self-assessment`, `internal`, `independent`). ASMT-007 holds both.
   - `preparation` (SP 800-53A section 3.1): `informed_by`, `officials_notified` (with the AO),
     `resources`, one `access` record for each of system, environment, documentation, records,
     artifacts and test-results, `documentation_provided`, the organizational `elements`,
     `channels` among the notified officials, `points_of_contact` outside the team, the
     `ambiguity_mechanism` between the organization and the assessors, and the `understanding`
     of the organization resting on ART-ORG-CONTEXT. ASMT-001 refuses anything dated after
     `schedule.start`. Why: an assessor who starts without these cannot finish.
   - `objectives`, `level_of_effort` and `approval` (`reviewed_by: PER-SCA`, `approved_by`
     PER-AO or PER-AODR, dated on or before `schedule.start`).
   - `procedures`: every scoped control in at least one record, each method applied to a
     control once, with the `methods` and `objects` chosen, `depth`, `coverage`, the
     `rationale`, `risk_results` naming ART-RA, `adaptation` (and `adaptation_note` when not
     `none`) and a `sequence`; procedures run together may share one. Several controls in one
     record consolidate them, such as one interview round for many controls beside each
     control's own examine and test record (ASMT-002). Interview applies to individuals;
     examine to specifications, mechanisms and activities; test to mechanisms and activities.
   - `rigor`: what the depth and coverage rest on (RIGR-001): `categorization: ART-CAT`,
     `privacy_risk_assessment: ART-RA` when the system processes PII, `plans` naming ART-SSP,
     the `assurance_requirements` the organization intends to meet (each `specified_by` a persona
     outside the team, with the least `depth` and `coverage` meeting it) and the `direction`
     (`by` outside the team, `conferred_with` on it, `factors`). Each procedure names its
     `assurance_requirement`, selects depth and coverage not below it, and carries one
     `sampling` record per method: the `types` sampled with a `number` each (personas for
     interview), `specific` objects under focused or comprehensive coverage, `selection`,
     `bias_control` unless random, and `extent` for mechanism tests (RIGR-003).
     Methods are not limited to the catalog's potential ones, and you need not use all of them.
     A-3 may use only the methods chosen here (ASMT-005). `optimization` records who reviewed
     the procedures to combine them, any tailoring guidance, and how they were ordered.
   - `additional_procedures`: procedures you develop for a requirement outside SP 800-53.
   - `reuse_policy`: the oldest result the organization lets you reuse (`max_age_days`), with
     `source: ART-ORG-CONTEXT`. `reused_results`: one record per result, with `id` (`RR-###`),
     `source`, `type`, the date `assessed`, `criteria`, `controls`, `independence`,
     `approved_by` (a user of the results, PER-AO or PER-AODR), `coordinated_with` (the system
     owner or CCP, and the AO or AODR), `determined_by` (an assessor), a `verdict` and `basis`
     for each of `credibility`, `appropriateness`, `applicability`, `currency` and `relevance`,
     `changes_since`, and `supplement` when more testing is needed. A `component-product`
     result also carries `product_review`. A result found `not-acceptable` is not reused
     (ASMT-003).
   - `external_providers`: one record for every boundary component with `external: true` and
     every leveraged authorization, named in `covers`, with the `arrangement`, the
     `agreement_review` by an assessor before approval, the `procedure_adjustment`, and the
     `provider_assessment` (scope, independence, who reviewed its procedures, `evidence`
     `received`, or still `requested` until A-4 or R-2 is in the run, never `refused`, whether
     it meets the protection needs, other assessments). A commercial or foreign government
     system outside USG authorities adds `third_party`, accepted by the AO or AODR. Why: the
     organization has less visibility here, so ASMT-004 refuses leveraging unseen results.
   - `schedule`: `start` and `end` dates after `run.yaml:as_of`, and `events` (kickoff,
     interviews, scans, test events reused, out-brief) with `kind` values from the schema.
   - `rules_of_engagement`: what the assessors may do on which systems, when, and who must
     be notified (scans on test units only, no testing on live networks without an IATT,
     and so on).
   - `penetration_test` whenever ca-8 is in the baseline or a cATO is sought or in force
     (and whenever the organization adds one, SP 800-53A Appendix D): the `scope` at its
     minimum (the environment subject to testing, the attack surface, the threat sources to
     simulate, the attacker's objectives, the level of effort sized to the cost and time
     available, the rules of engagement), the `components` tested, the `assessor`, and
     `guidance: NIST SP 800-115` (DoDI 8531.01); schedule it as a `penetration-test` event.
     When the authorization ledger holds an AD-CATO record (sought or in force), the test covers the `development` and `operational`
     `environments`, by a qualified third party, as a `cora` or `red-blue-team` `option`, or
     another kind under an approved `exception_to_policy` (PENT-001).
   - `sources`: the SCA's answers, the SSP artifact and the test-results passage.
   The reviewed controls in the OSCAL assessment plan are derived by `rmf build` from
   `baseline.json`, and its activities from `procedures`.
   - **`artifacts/data/test-strategy.yaml`** from `templates/data/test-strategy.yaml`, read from
     the TEMP or the test strategy the pathway calls for (EXT-TEST-STRATEGY): a TEMP on major
     capability acquisition, a test strategy on the MTA and software pathways, an abbreviated
     test plan or test strategy on urgent capability acquisition, the implementation plan of a
     business system (a TEMP when it is on the DOT&E oversight list). Record who approved each
     part: the DOT&E (or a designee) approves the OT&E and LFT&E planned activities of a program
     on T&E oversight, the USD(R&E) the DT&E plan of an ACAT ID program, the DoD Component the
     document; an oversight TEMP reaches the OSD 45 calendar days before the decision point it
     supports (TSTRAT-001). List each test event with the decision point it supports, what it
     evaluates, who conducts it, whether the testers are independent and threat representative,
     its resources, and the configuration and conditions under which its data is obtained. Plan
     cooperative vulnerability identification in DT, a CVPA, an adversarial assessment and an
     evaluation of defensive cyberspace operations in OT, a cyber economic vulnerability analysis
     when the system has financial functions, and independent threat-representative penetration
     and exploitation testing of the complete system cyberspace defenses, CSSP controls included,
     in both DT&E and OT&E (TSTRAT-002). Why: the assessment plan reuses these events, and A-3
     can reuse only what a production-representative system yielded (TSTRAT-003).
5. **Review and approval.** Interview PER-AODR to review the plan, then record the AO's
   approval (PER-AO, or PER-AODR if the AO delegated plan approval). In hybrid mode with a
   named human approver, the human must answer.
6. **Write `artifacts/ART-SAP.md`** from `templates/artifacts/ART-SAP.md`: scope and
   objectives, approach and methods, reuse of test results, team and independence,
   schedule, rules of engagement, and review and approval, each section traced.
   **Received systems.** For each system in `artifacts/data/reciprocity.yaml` `received_systems`, before the Receiving
   AO decides: situational awareness through eMASS or another tool, the package, deployment
   instructions and POA&M requested, the Granting decision reviewed (PER-AO or PER-AODR), and,
   unless the system is refused, this system's package shared, the deployment guide
   reviewed and the impact determined (through the DSAWG representative for an Enterprise
   system); augmenting controls are implemented by deployment. A pending system is judged only on
   the tests it records. Test by origin: a built-in control is not re-tested,
   one configured at deployment is tested by the receiving side once it is deployed, an inherited one is
   validated by the receiving ISO (PER-PM) with supporting evidence (RCP-004).

7. **Build and check.** `uv run rmf build <run>`, then `uv run rmf check <run> --task A-2`,
   until 0 errors.
8. **Journal** a DECISION for the approval and a CHECKPOINT.

## Interviews

| Persona | Why | Question focus |
|---|---|---|
| PER-SCA | responsible (R); plans the assessment | methods per control (examine, interview, test), depth and coverage, which developer or DT results to reuse, team independence, schedule, rules of engagement |
| PER-AODR | responsible (R); reviews for the AO | scope exclusions, sufficiency of methods for high-impact controls, schedule against milestones |
| PER-AO | accountable (A); approves the plan | approval, constraints |

At least 1 interview; this playbook expects PER-SCA and PER-AODR interviews, plus PER-AO
when the AO approves personally.

## Inputs

- `baseline.json`
- `artifacts/ART-SSP.md`, `artifacts/ssp/controls/*.yaml`
- `artifacts/ART-BASELINE.md`
- `artifacts/ART-RA.md` (risk results the tailoring applies)
- `artifacts/ART-ORG-CONTEXT.md` (the organization's operations and reuse policy)
- Assessment objectives: `uv run rmf catalog show --run <run> --fields title,objectives`
- `product/test-results.md` (test events and results available for reuse)

## Outputs

| File | Front-matter | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `artifacts/data/sap.yaml` | — | schema `sap` |
| `artifacts/ART-SAP.md` | `artifact_id: ART-SAP`, `produced_by_task: A-2`, `touched_by: [A-2]` | |

## Facts

A-2 writes no facts.

## Done when

- `sap.yaml` scopes the whole baseline (or excludes controls with rationale), names the team
  and schedule, and ART-SAP records the AO's approval.
- `uv run rmf check <run> --task A-2` reports 0 errors.

## Journal and lessons

- DECISION: `## <time> · DECISION · task A-2 · by: PER-AO (simulated, INT-###.A#)`.
- CHECKPOINT: `## <time> · CHECKPOINT · task A-2`.
